items.note: PDF text (dated April 2024) confirms: council vote March 2023, paid parking in force from 1 June 2024, Neudorf 'Zone Verte', 5h limit, charged 9h-19h Mon-Sat, Résipark 60 or 90 euros/month. The PDF has no title 'Stationnement payant au Neudorf'; its cover reads 'Quartier Neudorf - À compter du 1er juin 2024 - Nouvelles zones de stationnement payant'.
items.corrected_title: Quartier Neudorf : nouvelles zones de stationnement payant à compter du 1er juin 2024

items.note: Article (published 19 Sep 2024) says Eurométropole president Pia Imbs confirmed on 18 Sep at a press conference that the pedagogical period is extended so Crit'Air 3 may circulate until 31 Dec 2026 (initial plan was a ban at end-2024); Strasbourg is one of three large cities (with Marseille, Rouen) granted a ministry derogation. Title matches.

Page timetable: Crit'Air 5 enforced Jan 2023, Crit'Air 4 Jan 2024, Crit'Air 3 Jan 2027, Crit'Air 2 Jan 2028; Strasbourg, Schiltigheim, Ostwald and Holtzheim decided the 2028 Crit'Air 2 ban; 2024 and 2026 air-quality evaluations may adjust the calendar. Title matches.

Sud Radio article (6 Jul 2026) states abolition adopted in final vote 15 Apr 2026 in the loi de simplification de la vie économique; Constitutional Council removed it on 21 May 2026 (2026-903 DC) as a 'cavalier législatif' (procedure); ZFE remain in force and Strasbourg is listed among metropolises that kept theirs. Title matches.

strasbourg.eu article of 27 Nov 2025: new contract with SPL Parcus+voirie in force Monday 1 December, 15 years; previous contract delegated to Streeteo in 2018; exclusively public capital 95% City / 5% Eurométropole; Easypark and Indigo Neo kept; new Parcus+ app to be deployed in 2026. Title matches.

Decided, not merely announced: article (23 Jun 2026) says the two measures 'ont été votées en conseil municipal le 22 juin'. Resident permits 15/30/40 -> 5/10/20 euros/month from 1 July (tiers by quotient familial unique); from 1 September the visitor grid is capped at 17 euros for 3h red / 4h orange / 5h green; post-parking charge 17 euros if paid within three days, 35 euros thereafter. Title matches.

CTS page: 12 P+R, '+ de 4 000 places', day ticket 4.20 euros with unlimited bus+tram for 1 to 7 people, 24h 7.20 / 48h 14.40 / 72h 21.60, bus/tram subscribers free except Rotonde, Rotonde P+R subscription 66 euros/month. Title matches.

Page: 137 charge points in 12 Parcus+ car parks (list includes Gutenberg, Austerlitz, Opéra Broglie, Wodli, Gare courte durée); operation entrusted to Freshmile (IZIVIA only at Danube vert and Ste-Odile, not in the 12); 0.50/session + 0.60/kWh excluding parking cost, 'tarif en vigueur au 1er août 2022', except Wodli, Gare courte durée and Etoile Cinéma; Wodli/Gare courte durée have 0.50 + 0.49/kWh in force at 10 June 2026. Title matches.

Homepage: 'Parcus gère 18 parkings, dont 17 parkings souterrains et 1 parking fermé, d'une capacité totale de 10 000 places. En 2023 ... plus de 3 millions de clients horaires ... plus de 7 500 contrats d'abonnement.' Title matches.

Page: on 10 June 2026 SPL Parkings et Mobilités (Parcus+) took over operation of Parking Wodli (Bd du Président Wilson, direct access to platform 1 of the station) and the station Véloparc; 955 spaces on 11 levels, 42 EV-charging spaces. Title matches.

Page confirms closure since a fire on 1 May, favourable safety-commission opinion on 23 July allowing reopening, and Parcus+ takeover on 10 June. But it does not say repairs were done by Parcus+ (only that Parcus+ teams secured the site) and says the works were 'quasi achevés' (nearly complete). The page itself gives no year; 2026 is consistent with the Parcus Wodli page (takeover 10 June 2026).
items.corrected_text: The Gare courte durée car park, closed since a fire on 1 May, reopened to the public after a safety commission gave a favourable opinion on 23 July 2026, with repair works nearly complete. Parcus+ had taken over its operation on 10 June.

items.note: Dataset metadata via API: title 'Occupation en temps réel des parkings', publisher Eurométropole de Strasbourg, description 'places disponibles dans les parkings ouvragés', refreshed every 3 minutes, licence 'Licence Ouverte (Etalab)', records_count 35 on 2026-10-06.

Article published 29 Oct 2025 is forward-looking: tram F 'cheminera le 15 novembre prochain le long de huit nouvelles stations entre Strasbourg, Eckbolsheim et Wolfisheim'. Koenigshoffen is not named as served by the tram (only by bus C5 and a planned footbridge). P+R at the 'futur terminus' Wolfisheim Henri-Rendu with 100 car spaces and 50 bike spaces. (Item 13's source separately confirms Wolfisheim P+R opened 15 November.)
items.corrected_text: Tram line F was scheduled to run along eight new stations between Strasbourg, Eckbolsheim and Wolfisheim from 15 November 2025. The park-and-ride at the Wolfisheim Henri-Rendu terminus has 100 car spaces and 50 bike spaces.

items.note: Article of 12 Dec 2025 confirms all P+R saw higher use during the Christmas market and Wolfisheim (opened 15 Nov, 100 spaces) had high daily occupancy. Separating regular use from the Christmas peak is stated only for Wolfisheim, and the page speaks of 'mesures d'évolution adaptées' if necessary, not specifically capacity.
items.corrected_text: The Eurométropole reported that use of all its park-and-ride sites rose during the 2025 Christmas market and that the new Wolfisheim P+R (100 spaces, open since 15 November) had high daily occupancy. It said it was examining P+R use and, for Wolfisheim, would measure how much was due to the Christmas peak before taking adapted measures if needed.

items.note: Page title is 'How to park? | Noël à Strasbourg'. Text: on-street parking prohibited throughout Grande-Île 24/7 from 10:00 pm on November 25; 12 P+R at 4.20 euros. Year not in the sentence itself but the page references the 'Christmas 2025 guidebook' and Le Bonbon (item 15) gives the same 25 Nov 22h rule for 2025.

Le Bonbon article (29 Oct 2025, title matches): market 26 Nov-24 Dec 2025; Grande-Île 'interdite à la circulation' except emergency, public services and disabled-badge holders; Kléber, Gutenberg and Broglie car parks 'fermés au public et réservés uniquement aux abonnés disposant du fameux macaron' (subscribers holding the special pass). Forward-looking guide, which the text's 'reported ... would be' wording reflects.

Article of 21 Jan 2026: 2025 edition 3.05 million visitors, slightly below the 3.4 million of the previous edition 'qui avait atteint un record'; hotel occupancy close to 90% with guests from France, Germany, Spain, US, Japan, China, Turkey; Eurométropole residents made up half of visitors (sentence sits under a 'Village de l'Avent' subheading but is phrased generally). Title matches.

corrected_summary: Parcus reports managing 18 car parks with about 10,000 spaces in Strasbourg, and in June 2026 Parcus+ took over the Wodli and Gare courte durée station car parks; since 1 December 2025 paid on-street parking has been run by the public company SPL Parcus+voirie, replacing Streeteo. Paid on-street parking was extended to Neudorf in June 2024, the Crit'Air 3 restriction in the low-emission zone was moved to January 2027, and in June 2026 the city council cut resident permits to 5, 10 and 20 euros a month and capped visitor tariffs at 17 euros from September 2026. Tram F's extension to Wolfisheim, with a 100-space P+R, opened in November 2025, and the 2025 Christmas market drew 3.05 million visitors against a record 3.4 million the year before.
